trigger: name_identity casts const wchar_t* to const char16_t* with only a sizeof static_assert and no stated aliasing argument
policy_floor: routed-concern: C++ resource ownership and lifetime row (a cast rests on a proof stated at the site; docs/cpp-conventions.md)
classification_rationale: the proof a cast needs at its site is not written; the code itself is correct on MSVC
summary: Fixed: the site comment states that the translation unit is Windows-only and built with MSVC (wchar_t and char16_t are both unsigned 16-bit UTF-16 code units of equal size and alignment, no type-based alias analysis), that the view is read-only and does not outlive the call, and an alignof static_assert sits beside the sizeof one. One site serves read_key and, after G-3, prop_string.

trigger: prop_string converts the ETW ValueName with from_wide while the snapshot side stores names through registry_name_utf8, so a literal-U+FFFD name loses its writer match and a lone-surrogate write is matched to the writer of the distinct literal name U+FFFD+D800
classification_rationale: the documented writer lead is built from a different name identity than the row it explains, so a wrong process can be named as correct
summary: Fixed, not adjudicated down: name_identity moved above prop_string and the ETW name is built with name_identity(buf, wcsnlen(...)) before value_name_key, so both sides share one identity; a name holding U+0000 arrives cut and is not attributed (stated at the site). Portable correlation cases pin a literal U+FFFD name, a lone surrogate against a literal U+FFFD+D800 name written by two processes, and an ASCII name. The prop_string line is Windows-only: its evidence is the kingsley compile and the existing live attribution cases.

trigger: 32 denied names already stored, then a read with a first or larger skipped_overflow: no new name, so no gap row, and the count was never persisted
classification_rationale: the documented rule is that growth of the blind area writes a gap row; the code wrote one only for a new named child
summary: Fixed: RegistryRootState gains skipped_overflow (optional on decode, written only when above zero, so existing cursor rows stay byte-identical). An increase is a gain; a Capped read keeps the larger of stored and read, any other read sets it; the Unreadable branch leaves it alone. Persisted because the cursor commits with the row. A new status key was declined: the gap row already carries the count and a new key is a new public contract.

summary: Adversarial-review gate (report not committed). Same defect as S-1, fixed once there, with the 32 to 33 and 33 to 34 multi-tick cases it asked for.

trigger: same as S-1 (first overflow after 32 already-known skipped names)
summary: Spec axis of the code-review gate (report not committed) asked whether a newly non-zero or larger overflow is a gain. It is; fixed with S-1.

trigger: an operator reads the README, user manual or echo.json: 'the first 32 are named in the row', while the row names three, then '+n more', then 'and n more not named'; docs/echo-implementer.md still says the 33rd child makes the read Capped
classification_rationale: the docs state a row content the code does not produce
summary: Fixed (docs only): the row names the first three and counts the rest; the reader tracks up to 32 by name per root, counts the others (and n more not named) while the walk goes on; a row is written when a tracked child is new or the untracked count grows. docs/echo-implementer.md rewritten for the counted 33rd child, NUL-named children taking the same path unopened, the skip path charged to the key budget and deadline, names through registry_name_utf8, and the persisted overflow count. echo.json regenerated with plugin_doc_gen.py --all; --check clean.

trigger: the overflow-means-no-removal rule, the legacy single-U+FFFD baseline and the budget wiring were unpinned on macOS; the Windows live cases SKIP when HKLM is not writable
classification_rationale: tests that pin shipped behaviour are missing
summary: Fixed in part, by ruling: the no-removal rule now holds where removals are derived (the diff treats a read with skipped_overflow above zero as non-authoritative, whatever its status) with a pure case; the legacy single-U+FFFD baseline has a pure case on a Complete and a Capped read. Declined by ruling: a forced name collision and the skip-path budget wiring, which are not reachable without a new seam; the budget decision itself is the pure admit_key_by case. The three [windows] live cases keep the existing SKIP convention; the PR body states the kingsley result per case.

trigger: a root that stays Capped only adds, so the old single-U+FFFD entry is not reported removed until a complete read; an earlier build also stored another key's values under a NUL-named child's path
classification_rationale: 'reported once as removed and added' is not what a permanently Capped root does
summary: Fixed (docs only): the changelog, README and manual now say the name is reported as added under its new stored form and the old form as removed at the next complete read of that root, as a change of stored name and not of the host; values an earlier build stored under a NUL-named child are kept, unreported, while that child exists (adapted from 'until the root is purged': a deleted child's entries are reported removed by the next complete read, as for a denied child). The gap-row text change ('denied read access or not openable') is added to the changelog.

trigger: no test pins the documented upgrade behaviour for a baseline holding a value under a single U+FFFD

summary: Functional axis of the code-review gate (report not committed). Fixed with S-3: a pure diff case, a Complete read yields one removed and one added row, a Capped read yields only the added row.
